rationale: The target buyer — 'non-programmer knowledge workers' who want local, private AI — is too vague to sell to reliably, and the willingness-to-pay signal is thin (a single HN post from a builder, no confirmed revenue). More critically, the product itself is a desktop client with local inference, which Claude + this repo cannot build or deliver: it requires native OS packaging, local model management, and per-device installation, making both buildability and operational autonomy near-zero. The problem exists, but this is not something a solo non-technical operator can build or run hands-off.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for this factory. A local desktop AI client requires native application development (OS packaging, signed installers, local model downloads) that goes far beyond what Claude + a landing page + Stripe can deliver. Even if built, distribution and support would be per-device, per-user manual work. Drop and do not pursue.
notes: Fails build_gates: operational_autonomy=3 (below 7 floor), buildability_with_ai=3 (below 6 floor), buyer_clarity=4 (below 6 floor), willingness_to_pay=4 (below 5 floor). Total also below validate threshold.
